title: Evaluation of a cartesian algebra-diagram adjunction respects counits and coefficient restriction
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism between topoi presented by sites small in the module universe, let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $J$ be a small category [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B_Y:J\to\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y))$ be a diagram of commutative algebras over the constant sheaf $\underline A_Y$, and set $B_X=u^{-1}B_Y$, with the induced algebra structures and all actual diagram transitions. Use the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_A^J(T)$ for the derived category of $J$-diagrams of $\underline A_T$-modules and $D_B(T)$ for the derived category of semilinear $B_T$-module diagrams. Let $U_T:D_B(T)\to D_A^J(T)$ be exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and let $G_A\dashv P_A$, $G_B\dashv P_B$ be the canonical derived diagram inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. The structural coefficient maps for $u$ are isomorphisms, so $G_A,G_B$ are exact inverse images.
All derived adjunctions below are induced from the module adjunctions. For $j\in J$ let $e^B_{T,j}:D_B(T)\to D(B_{T,j})$ and $e^A_{T,j}:D_A^J(T)\to D(\underline A_T)$ be exact evaluations. Write $G_j\dashv P_j$ for the canonical derived adjunction on $B_{T,j}$-coefficients, $G\dashv P$ for that on constant-$A$ coefficients, and $U_{T,j}$ for restriction from $B_{T,j}$ to $\underline A_T$. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$\lambda_j:e^B_{X,j}G_B\xrightarrow{\sim}G_j e^B_{Y,j},\qquad \beta_j:e^B_{Y,j}P_B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j e^B_{X,j},\qquad \delta_j:e^A_{Y,j}P_A\xrightarrow{\sim}P e^A_{X,j}.$$
The left comparison is localization of the componentwise inverse-image identification; the right comparisons use the derived adjunctions induced from the module evaluation adjunctions. If $\varepsilon_B,\varepsilon_j$ are the indicated counits, then
$$e^B_{X,j}(\varepsilon_{B,N})=\varepsilon_{j,e^B_{X,j}N}\,G_j(\beta_{j,N})\,\lambda_{j,P_BN}.$$
Equivalently, for every $t:M\to P_BN$ with transpose $t^\flat:G_BM\to N$,
$$(\beta_{j,N}e^B_{Y,j}(t))^\flat=e^B_{X,j}(t^\flat)\lambda_{j,M}^{-1}.$$
Let $d:U_YP_B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_AU_X$ and $d_j:U_{Y,j}P_j\xrightarrow{\sim}PU_{X,j}$ be the canonical coefficient-restriction/direct-image comparisons, normalized by the common derived-composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Under $e^A_{T,j}U_T=U_{T,j}e^B_{T,j}$ their compatibility is the equality
$$\delta_{j,U_XN}\,e^A_{Y,j}(d_N)=d_{j,e^B_{X,j}N}\,U_{Y,j}(\beta_{j,N}).$$
These comparisons are natural in $N$ and in the semilinear diagram transitions (after the corresponding restrictions of scalars). No preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation, coefficient flatness, perfectness or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the normalized ordinary evaluation and coefficient restriction comparisons and the inverse-image mate, including its ordinary counit equation.
Use exact scalar restriction and the common-composite right-derived normalization to construct d, dj and the comparisons for ring-transition restriction.

The free diagram left adjoint is the coproduct over arrows from the vertex and is exact in the Grothendieck category of module sheaves. Thus constant-ring evaluation preserves K-injectives. Derived comparison existence gives delta.

On a K-injective B-diagram, coefficient acyclicity gives invertibility of the fA right-derived unit after total restriction. The normalized constant-evaluation square transports this invertibility to the s unit at the constant evaluation. The vertex restriction square and conservativity of exact scalar restriction then give invertibility of the fj unit at the varying evaluation. Apply normalized derived-square existence to construct beta.

Apply unit-normalized derived comparison coherence to obtain the counit, arbitrary transpose, coefficient cube and both actual-arrow transition equations, and assemble the original existential assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-ba04423f6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: the statement is unchanged and the proof is 8 steps (7606 characters) with no new nodes. Shape: one commit touching only the item and its report; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; the dependency closure (252 nodes) has no cycle; there is no SGA source. The item has no re-split note and is not in any dropped list. Live and side-live still show it unsplit, so the delivery is not superseded. Sources checked: Stacks sites-cohomology 07A6 lemma-adjoint (l.3990), 0D6E lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (l.4011) and 0941 lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (l.5067); 0941 concerns constant abelian towers only, and the proof correctly does not use it for varying rings. Step 1 unpacks the varying-ring diagram site, which is elementary; restriction of scalars reflects quasi-isomorphisms because it keeps the underlying abelian sheaf. Step 2: the free-diagram left adjoint L_j is exact (finite subsums plus exact filtered colimits in a Grothendieck category), so constant-A evaluation preserves K-injectives by right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective; the hypotheses of exact-square-derived-counit hold. Step 3: the composition normalization (f = restriction along ΔA_X→B_X, g = u) gives d_QI = Qf_A(a), and f(c) gives d_j. Step 4 is the key step and I verified it: H_j is K-injective; h·a_j ≃ cU(b) by the K-injective Hom bijection; two-out-of-three on f(h)f(a_j) = f(c)f(Ub) makes f_j(b) a quasi-isomorphism, so η_{f_j,I_j} is invertible without claiming I_j is K-injective. This is sound for non-flat transitions such as ℤ→ℤ/2. Step 5: β is defined by η-normalization; it is natural and resolution-independent by kinjective-derived-map-computation. Step 6: the Hom formula of exact-square-derived-counit, specialized to identities, pins both adjunctions and gives the transpose identity and the counit identity e(ε_B) = ε_j·G_j(β)·λ in the printed directions; this makes β the mate of λ. Step 7: both sides are represented by Qf(a_j) and Qf(cUb), and the identification uses the unique transition class k = h. Step 8: the transitions go through η_{f_j,r_X I_k}, which is invertible by step 4 at k and the composition normalization; the δ case is the special case B = ΔA, and d is automatically compatible with transitions. Edge cases checked: empty J, J = {∗}, discrete J, parallel arrows, monoid categories, zero ring. I accept the worker-written tool_uses (generic K-injective, derived-functor and ringed-topos tools).
